text: dsh-claude-bridge 是面向 DSH 的 Claude 模型提供方插件，通过 Claude Code CLI 与 Agent SDK 接入 Claude Pro 或 Max 订阅。它向 DSH 注册 claude-bridge 路由，提供模型列表、模型解析、流式文本与推理响应，并将 DSH 工具通过进程内 MCP 服务交给 CLI，支持多轮工具调用。适合希望在 DSH 中使用已登录 Claude 账户的用户；使用前须先完成 Claude Code 登录。

dsh-claude-bridge connects Claude models to DSH through Claude Code and the Agent SDK, using an existing Claude Pro or Max login. It registers a model provider, lists models, streams answers, and relays DSH tools through MCP for multi-round calls.
想让 DSH 的 agent 使用我已登录的 Claude 订阅模型。
如何把 Claude Code 提供的模型接入 DSH 的模型列表？
I want DSH agents to stream Claude answers and use the tools I provide.
dsh-claude-bridge 的功能「Claude 模型路由」：在 DSH 注册 claude-bridge 提供方，列出并解析内置 Claude 模型，供 agent 按提供方 ID 选择。
dsh-claude-bridge 的功能「流式生成与工具调用」：将对话交给 Claude Code CLI，流式返回文本、推理和工具调用，并通过 MCP 将 DSH 工具结果送回 CLI。
dsh-claude-bridge 使用前须知：需要先在 Claude Code 登录；CLI 会读取该登录凭据文件，插件本身不提供登录流程。

dsh-claude-bridge README · dsh-claude-bridge：Use a Claude Pro or Max subscription as a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) model provider, by driving the Claude Code CLI through the Agent SDK.

dsh-claude-bridge README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-claude-bridge
```

Restart `dsh`. It registers one provider route, `claude-bridge`, and does not disable anything: it sits beside whatever else serves models and is chosen per agent by provider id.

dsh-claude-bridge README · Install：You need to be signed in to Claude Code already. This bridge does not authenticate: it runs a CLI
that reads the credential `claude` login wrote, at `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (or
`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json`). Sign in with `claude` in a terminal, then `/login` there.

The CLI it runs is the one bundled with the Agent SDK, not whatever `claude` is on your PATH; PATH is
not consulted. Only the credential file is shared. Set `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` to run a
different binary.

dsh-claude-bridge README · Install：Settings are not read off disk. The child loads no user, project or local `settings.json`, so your own
hooks, plugins and skills stay out of it, and a stray `env` block cannot move the route off your plan.

dsh-claude-bridge README · Why not just sign in to Anthropic：The harness can already do that, and it works. [`dsh-provider-login`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-provider-login) reaches the OAuth flow labelled "Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max)" that the harness registers.
section: Why not just sign in to Anthropic

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · Why not just sign in to Anthropic：The difference is billing, not capability. Per Pi's documentation of the same underlying library, third-party harness usage through that route **draws from extra usage and is billed per token, not against Claude plan limits**. Driving the CLI through the Agent SDK is the mechanism that lands usage on the plan instead.
section: Why not just sign in to Anthropic

text:
dsh-claude-bridge README · Why not just sign in to Anthropic：That ground is not perfectly settled: Anthropic [announced and then unannounced](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15036540-use-the-claude-agent-sdk-with-your-claude-plan) a change to how Agent SDK usage is billed. Know that before you depend on it.

This approach is not original. It is the same one [`pi-claude-bridge`](https://github.com/elidickinson/pi-claude-bridge) takes for the Pi agent, by Eli Dickinson, which is where the design here comes from.
section: Why not just sign in to Anthropic

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：**Works.** Streaming text and reasoning; **tool calls**, including multi-round conversations; token usage with cache reads and writes; finish reasons; model listing and resolution; reasoning effort; and the one-million-token window as an opt-in.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：Tools are the interesting part, because the two sides disagree about who blocks. The harness treats a tool round as two calls: `stream()` ends with a `tool-calls` finish, the harness runs the tools, and it calls `stream()` again with the results appended. The CLI treats the same round as one call that never ended: it invokes a tool and its query sits blocked inside that handler.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：So the query is not closed when the first `stream()` returns. It is parked, with the handler still awaiting, and resumed when the results arrive. The harness's tools reach the CLI over an in-process MCP server, with their JSON Schemas served verbatim rather than round-tripped through Zod, which loses everything below the top level. Calls are paired to results by the tool-use id the CLI stamps on each request, because call order is not promised to match the order the blocks were emitted.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：A result can also arrive before the CLI has got round to asking for it, so delivery and waiting are decoupled: whichever comes second finds the other. Assuming an order there deadlocks the pair.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：What a parked round is waiting for is the set of calls the adapter reported to the harness, not the set the child has dispatched. Those differ on every parallel round, because the child dispatches its calls one at a time while the harness answers all of them in one message. Gating on the dispatched set drops the answers to the rest, and nothing carries them again.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：**A named limitation on history.** The CLI owns its own session history, and the faithful way to carry a conversation into it is to write its session file and resume. This build states the turns inline in the prompt instead. The model sees the whole conversation, but the CLI's prefix cache sees a new one each turn: correct, and expensive, in that order. Within a single tool round the query stays open, so that round does reuse the cache.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：**Cancelling.** The harness cancels by abandoning the stream, so that is where the child is ended: the abort reaches it directly rather than only through a control request it has to be well enough to answer, and an interrupt that is not acknowledged within five seconds stops being waited on. Otherwise a cancelled turn keeps running to completion, on your plan.
section: What works, and what does not

text: dsh-claude-bridge README · What works, and what does not：**Concurrency.** Sessions are held per harness session id, but a call that offers no tools never takes one: with no MCP server it cannot park, so it runs detached and cannot evict a round parked under the same id. The shipped session-title provider issues exactly that call, concurrently, under the live turn's own id.
section: What works, and what does not

dsh-claude-bridge README · Configuration：Some decisions are taken for you and are not options. The CLI child runs with `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=0` and `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1`, its preset is told to exclude `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules`, and it loads no settings files at all. Each hands a decision back to the harness that the CLI would otherwise make for itself: the harness owns tool discovery, compaction, and context files.

dsh-claude-bridge README · Configuration：The variables that would move the child onto a different account, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, are removed from its environment rather than forwarded. The harness materializes `<cwd>/.env` and `$DSH_HOME/.env` into its own environment before any plugin loads, so one of these left in a `.env` for another tool would otherwise reach the child and bill per token.

dsh-claude-bridge README · Development：```sh
npm run check   # typecheck
npm test        # the gate suite
npm run build   # emit lib/
```

The suite covers the orderings the two sides can arrive in, which is where every real defect here has been. The adapter tests replace the CLI but not its tool calls: a genuine MCP client drives the server the adapter builds, through the same handler and the same tool-use id pairing the CLI uses.
